column1: # The source the lease candidate closure is built from and what the built
# closure turned out to be, recorded so the identity is read rather than
# re-derived. Every value names where it was read: the source rows from git in
# the pinned checkout, the applied lists from the apply sequence itself, the
# promoted and candidate marker rows from strings(1) over each closure's
# llama-server and libllama-server-impl.so, the threshold rows from each
# closure's CMakeCache.txt, the payload rows from each build log, and the
# promoted arch and payload from scripts/serving-closures.tsv.
# The applied order is verify-llama-patch-series.sh's own: the six production
# patches, then the candidates in ledger order, with the two this closure leaves
# out named as omitted. The three headers the Vulkan production patches add are
# staged, since the builder refuses an untracked source file and git diff HEAD
# What the comparison establishes is narrow. The two closures agree on
# architecture, cubin and ptx counts, both MMVQ thresholds, and the absence of
# the paged-KV and device-embedding markers, and each lease marker below is read
# on both sides. It does not establish source equivalence: a marker absent from
# a binary states that one patch's strings are absent rather than that no other
# The promoted closure's own source_diff_sha256 is 0d6e3be391768d5b0aaa8854904b
# and four reconstructions from today's patch files reproduce none of it: the
# production series alone, plus view-alias-deps, plus mmvq-crossover, and plus
# paged-kv and mtmd-embd read ed47ca4c, ed957fe7, f0f1e551, 3e47e7a1, and
# 9a75d608 respectively. Which patch file moved since that build is unread here,
# so the promoted set is named by the markers and thresholds its binaries carry
# rather than by a replayed diff.
